DERIVATION: the .do imports 3508_num.csv (header cells 'NAME: label'), renames each variable to the text before ':', lowercases, and Bookmark 7 sets item = the literal lowercased CIS names p15, p15a, p15b -- core model s3 pattern 1, Step 5b exempt, no verification_/verify_ files written. LABELS: cues3508.pdf prints each question immediately followed by its own tag [P15] / [P15A] / [P15B] (asserted as exact substrings 'P.15 <stem> [P15] (CATEGORÍA NOMINAL) Sí' etc. of the whitespace-normalised pdftotext -raw text in .cache/spain_2026_love_usage/build.R); ES3508 VARIABLE LABELS are CIS summaries, not shipped, and agree in content under the same code: P15 'Conocimiento de las aplicaciones de citas y para ligar (Tinder, Badoo, Grindr o Meetic)', P15A 'Creación de perfil en alguna aplicación de citas y para ligar', P15B 'Tenencia de alguna cita con alguien conocido en una aplicación de citas y para ligar'. VALUE LABELS: P15 1 'Sí' 2 'No' 8 'N.S.' 9 'N.C.'; P15A and P15B the same plus 0 'N.P.' = the printed options. There is NO code 3 ('Regular') in this battery (0 occurrences in the data). FILTERS (printed skips, confirmed in the data): 'Si P15=(2;8;9) ir a [P17]' -- P15A=0 N.P. iff P15 != 1 (398/398, 0 off-diagonal); 'Si P15A=(2;8;9) ir a [P16_1]' -- P15B=0 N.P. iff P15A != 1 (3,658/3,658, 0 off-diagonal). So p15 was asked of all 5,007, p15a of the 4,609 who had heard of dating apps, p15b of the 1,349 who had created a profile. REBUILD, decisive: reading 3508_num.csv (5,007 records; id = row number), setting p15 8/9 and p15a/p15b 0/8/9 to missing as the .do does, cov_sex = SEXO (Hombre/Mujer in live), cov_age = EDAD (999 -> NA) reproduces the live table exactly: 10,959 rows both, 5,003 ids both, 0 only-rebuilt / 0 only-live, 0 resp / cov_sex / cov_age mismatches, 0 duplicate id-item keys (.cache/spain_2026_love_usage/rebuild.R, rebuild.log; live via irw_fetch served from the local irw cache written by table_context.R). ANTI-SWAP: relabelling p15a<->p15b gives 3,258 only-alt / 3,258 only-live keys and 582 resp mismatches. Live item x resp (1 Sí / 2 No): p15 4609/394; p15a 1349/3258; p15b 1058/291 -- every item uses both levels and each has an option row. DROPPED TO MISSING by the .do: p15 8 N.S. 3 / 9 N.C. 1 (4); p15a 0 N.P. 398 / 9 N.C. 2 (no 8); p15b 0 N.P. 3,658 (no 8/9). The 4 p15 N.S./N.C. respondents are also N.P. on p15a/p15b, hence 5,003 of 5,007 ids. TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = each printed question verbatim from cues3508.pdf ('P.15 '/'P.15a '/'P.15b ' numbering stripped, line wraps joined); P.15a and P.15b open with 'Y' continuing P.15 and are shipped as printed. Three standalone questions with no shared prompt, so instructions and section_prompt are blank, one trivial section (the spain_2026_love_gestures shape). The skip lines are routing, not read to respondents, and are not shipped as text; they are disclosed in public_note. option_text = 'Sí'/'No' = value labels 1/2. translation_source=machine_translation: CIS publishes Estudio 3508 in Spanish only; the _translated columns were written by IRW, 'aplicaciones de citas y para ligar' rendered 'dating and hookup apps' as in spain_2026_love_apps. STEP 3b: dictionary Description 'Awareness of, profile creation on, and dating through apps' matches P.15/P.15a/P.15b; the .do comment names P15, P15A, P15B and live has exactly those three codes. No instrument mismatch. DICTIONARY DEFECT (already logged in batch_375; not fixed here): the dictionary Reference reads 'Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS), Percepción de la prostitución, Estudio 3508', but Estudio 3508 is 'Percepción social del amor'. RIGHTS: no block; applied the existing instrument_rights_register.csv CIS row (line 117, verdict allow, every CIS survey year); originator is CIS. No register row written. SIBLINGS: no other spain_2026_love_* table touched; the apps cache was only read, all scratch under .cache/spain_2026_love_usage/.
public_note: The English in the _translated columns was machine-translated by IRW from the Spanish CIS administered (CIS publishes this questionnaire in Spanish only); the items are a filtered sequence -- p15 was asked of everyone, p15a only of the 4,609 respondents who had heard of dating apps, and p15b only of the 1,349 who had created a profile -- so later items cover smaller subsets; resp 1 is 'yes' and 2 'no', and 'don't know'/'no answer' (6 responses) are missing.
